cf.title: Fall back to serializing when parallel apply runs out of DSM segments

input.subject: [PATCH] Fall back to serializing when parallel apply runs out of DSM segments

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. Both patches pass a flag that InitializeParallelDSM() already passes, so existing NULL checks and the documented streaming = parallel fallback become reachable. Message #1 gives a reproduction, which P4 and P5 lacked. Confidence is medium because the code was not read and the callers of make_new_segment() were not checked.

brief.title: Use the serialize fallback when parallel apply runs out of DSM segments
brief.problem: With streaming = parallel, the leader apply worker errors out when no DSM segment is free, because dsm_create() raises "too many dynamic shared memory segments" instead of returning NULL. The worker restarts and fails at the same STREAM START, so the subscription makes no progress until segments are freed. The same flaw makes DSA_ALLOC_NO_OOM raise an error instead of returning InvalidDsaPointer.
brief.proposed_design: 0001 passes DSM_CREATE_NULL_IF_MAXSEGMENTS in pa_setup_dsm(), as InitializeParallelDSM() does. The existing fallback then runs, and the leader serializes the streamed transaction to a file and applies it itself. 0002 passes the same flag in make_new_segment() in dsa.c, so the existing NULL check there is reached.
user_visible_surface: Behavior change: with streaming = parallel, running out of DSM segments now spills the transaction to temporary files instead of failing the apply worker.
C API behavior change: dsa_allocate_extended() with DSA_ALLOC_NO_OOM returns InvalidDsaPointer when DSM segments run out, instead of raising an ERROR.
author_claims: The patch makes the server match the documented streaming = parallel fallback to temporary files.
In a test that held all DSM slots, master restarted the apply worker 13 times in a minute with nothing applied; the patch applied all rows.
Without 0002, callers such as pgstat_get_entry_ref() and pg_stash_advice skip their cleanup when DSM segments run out.
The flaw dates from 216a784829c; 0001 applies to 16 and later, and 0002's code is the same on all supported branches.
The author first proposed backpatching 0001 to 16 and 0002 to 14.
brief.thread_state: Zhijie Hou and Bharath Rupireddy both approve the patches; v2 drops a comment change at Hou's request. Bharath argues for HEAD only because the case is rare and unreported, the author accepts that, and the backpatch decision is left to a committer.
unclear: Neither patch lists a test file, so no regression test covers the out-of-segments path; the repro used an external test extension.
The thread does not say whether every caller of make_new_segment() handles a NULL segment correctly once that path becomes reachable.
The thread does not say whether other dsm_create() callers have the same unreachable NULL check.
Hou wrote "other caller of pa_setup_dsm() in dsa.c"; the author read this as make_new_segment(), and Hou did not confirm.
The thread does not say what pg_stash_advice is or where it lives.

precedents_retrieved.title: DSA Hash Tables (DHT): hash tables backed by DSM segments
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a general-purpose hash table in DSA memory, so several backends can share it and it can grow, along the lines of dynahash. It uses separate chaining, incremental resizing, partition-based locking and concurrent iteration.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author parked the patch after its only planned user, Dilip Kumar's Parallel Bitmap Heap Scan, stopped using it. He did not expect a committer to take it without a concrete user, which Andres Freund had asked for at the start. Reviewers found no problems with the design.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improving the latch handling between logical replication launcher and worker processes.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a lost wakeup in the logical replication launcher, which uses one latch for worker attach, worker exit and subscription creation, so a new subscription's apply worker can wait up to 180 seconds to start. The author listed three options and posted v2 using a separate latch for worker attach and exit, protected by a lock and owned only around each wait.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not state a closing reason. Kyotaro Horiguchi objected to v2 because it calls OwnLatch and DisownLatch often and nests latch waits across concurrent wakeup sources, and he proposed a flag in shared memory that ApplyLauncherMain checks before WaitLatch. The author agreed and posted a new patch for that approach, and Heikki Linnakangas noted that his proposed interrupts patches would make the fix simple. The thread ends there without a review of the new patch.
matched_queries: logical replication apply worker restart loop
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Additionally, handling multiple concurrently operating trigger sources with nested latch waits seems bug-prone, which I’d prefer to avoid from both a readability and safety perspective.

precedents_retrieved.title: Implement NULL-related checks in object address functions to prevent cache lookup errors
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set makes the SQL functions pg_describe_object, pg_identify_object and pg_identify_object_as_address return NULL for undefined objects instead of raising "cache lookup failed" errors. It adds missing_ok flags to getObjectDescription, getObjectIdentity and lower-level lookup routines such as get_attname, GetForeignServer and the publication and subscription lookups.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Several preparatory patches were committed during the thread, but the main objectaddress patch was not. In its last review, Alvaro Herrera found that pg_identify_object returned an empty type in only some cases, and that it reported a column for a relation with no such column. The author fixed the column case, but left open whether type, operator and function formatting should be reworked to return NULL for undefined objects. The visible messages show no reply after that, and no closing message.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: One thing is that I am not sure if it is worth complicating the existing interface even more just to deal with undefined objects as pure NULLs.

precedents_retrieved.title: Apply a better fix to mdunlinkfork().
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Apply a better fix to mdunlinkfork().
Reverted commit(s): Use TRUNCATE to preserve relfilenode for pg_largeobject + index.; Fix failure to remove non-first segments of temporary tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Replace the stopgap fix I made in 0e758ae89 with a cleaner one.

The real problem with 4ab5dae94 is that it contorted this function's
logic substantially, by introducing a third code path that required
different behavior in the function's main loop.  That seems quite
unnecessary on closer inspection: the new IsBinaryUpgrade case can
just share the behavior of the other immediate-unlink cases.  Hence,
revert 4ab5dae94 and most of 0e758ae89 (keeping the latter's
save/restore errno fix), and add IsBinaryUpgrade to the set of
conditions tested to choose immediate unlink.

Also fix some additional places with sloppy handling of errno,
to ensure we have an invariant that we always continue processing
after any non-ENOENT failure of do_truncate.  I doubt that that's
fixing any bug of field importance, so I don't feel it necessary to
back-patch; but we might as well get it right while we're here.

Also improve the comments, which had drifted a bit from what the
code actually does, and neglected to mention some important
considerations.

Back-patch to v15, not because this is fixing any bug but because
it doesn't seem like a good idea for v15's mdunlinkfork logic to be
significantly different from both v14 and v16.

precedents_retrieved.title: Apply worker fails if a relation is missing on subscriber even if refresh publication has not been refreshed yet
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch would let the logical replication apply worker skip changes for tables that were added to a publication but are not yet in pg_subscription_rel on the subscriber, because ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION has not been run. It would log a warning instead of failing repeatedly when such a table is missing on the subscriber.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila questioned whether the current ERROR behavior should be changed when no specific use case had been given. He noted that users can avoid the failure loop with the disable_on_error subscription parameter, and that silently skipping changes could surprise users whose subscriber-side setup is incomplete. The author said he had no specific use case, and the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I see your point but not sure if it is worth changing the

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve monitoring of shared memory allocations
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_shmem_allocations show the full size of shared hash tables by allocating the header, directory, segments and elements in one ShmemInitStruct() call in hash_create(). It also replaces most ShmemAlloc() calls with named ShmemInitStruct() allocations so they are tracked.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The first two parts were committed and then reverted after a bug in non-shared hash tables: dir_realloc() freed a directory that was no longer allocated on its own, which caused a pfree error. Tomas Vondra did not push the fix for shared hash tables only into PG18, because dynahash is critical and its tests never run dir_realloc(). He and Amit Kapila asked for better test coverage first. The author did not add the tests, and Heikki Linnakangas later closed the entry as superseded by commit 9fe9ecd516.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow to warn or error on ... = NULL expressions
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend the transform_null_equals setting from a boolean to an enum with off, warn, error and on values, so that "expr = NULL" expressions can produce a warning or the SQL-standard error. The original patch made 'warn' the default; later versions kept the existing behaviour as the default.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas objected to making 'warn' the default because "foo = NULL" is legal SQL, and saw little value in the warn mode, since such queries can be found with grep. Bruce Momjian considered this one check not useful enough on its own and wanted it to be part of a wider "novice" mode that warns about bad SQL practices. Dmitry Dolgov asked what such a mode should include, received no response, and marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I will again say I would love to see this as part of a wholesale
"novice" mode which warns of generally bad SQL practices.  I don't see
this one item alone as sufficiently useful.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found for this idea. P4 and P5 died for lack of a reproduction, and message #1 supplies one. Its repro used an external extension, and the patches add no in-tree regression test; that is a level 4 matter, outside this angle.

Both patches make the server follow the contract already in the docs: the streaming = parallel fallback to temporary files, and InvalidDsaPointer under DSA_ALLOC_NO_OOM. No syntax, GUC, catalog, pg_dump or psql surface changes, and only callers that already handle the documented failure value see new behavior. Back-patching 0002 to minor releases would let extension callers reach their NULL-handling paths for the first time, but the thread now proposes HEAD only, and whether those paths are correct is a code question.

Neither patch changes on-disk format, WAL, catalogs, the wire protocol or struct layouts. 0001 sends the leader into the existing serialize-to-file fallback, which already runs when no parallel apply worker is free; 0002 lets DSA_ALLOC_NO_OOM callers get the InvalidDsaPointer result their contract already promises. Not checkable without code: whether every make_new_segment() caller handles NULL.

Both patches add DSM_CREATE_NULL_IF_MAXSEGMENTS so an existing NULL check becomes reachable; nothing changes who may do what or see what. Running out of DSM segments now spills to the same temporary files that streaming = on already uses, so no new disk-use or denial-of-service path for unprivileged users appears.

Both patches add a flag that parallel query already passes to dsm_create(), so existing NULL checks and the documented fallback to temporary files become reachable. Nothing new is added on a common path, and there is no new API, GUC or dependency. Without the code I cannot confirm that every make_new_segment() caller handles a NULL segment.

This is a bug fix that makes existing fallback code reachable, using the flag DSM_CREATE_NULL_IF_MAXSEGMENTS that InitializeParallelDSM() already passes. It adds no mechanism, and no existing feature or extension meets the need in its place, so there is nothing to raise from the already-exists angle.

Demand is not the right test for this proposal. It is a small bug fix that makes streaming = parallel match its documented fallback to temporary files, and it makes the existing NULL checks in pa_setup_dsm() and make_new_segment() reachable. The thread's own concern about demand (message #4: rare, not reported from the field) was settled by applying the fix to HEAD only, which the author accepted in message #5. Unlike [P4] and [P5], the author gave a reproduction: on master the apply worker restarted 13 times in a minute with nothing applied, and with the patch all rows were applied. The cost falls only on the out-of-segments path, so users who never reach it pay nothing. One question is for other panel members: whether every caller of make_new_segment() handles a NULL segment once 0002 makes that path reachable.
